foods.notes: Made from apples and pears — both high FODMAP fruits. Belgian specialty but avoid.

foods.name: pesto (commercial)
foods.notes: Usually contains garlic. Check label or make homemade with garlic-infused oil.
alternatives: homemade pesto with garlic-infused oil, basil, pine nuts, parmesan

foods.name: curry paste (Thai)
foods.notes: Often contains garlic and onion. Small amounts may be tolerated. Check label.

foods.name: sambal oelek
foods.notes: Some brands contain garlic. Pure chili sambal is low FODMAP.

foods.name: balsamic vinegar
foods.notes: Low FODMAP in normal serving sizes.

foods.name: coconut aminos
foods.notes: Low FODMAP soy sauce alternative. Slightly sweeter flavor.

foods.name: Dijon mustard
foods.notes: Low FODMAP. Belgian favorite condiment.

foods.name: hot sauce (Tabasco-style)
foods.notes: Most hot sauces made from chili, vinegar, and salt are low FODMAP. Check for garlic.

foods.name: kombucha
foods.notes: Low FODMAP up to about 180ml. Higher amounts may have excess fructose depending on brand.

foods.name: cranberry juice
foods.notes: Low FODMAP. Good juice option.

foods.name: hot chocolate (with regular milk)
foods.notes: High lactose from milk. Use lactose-free milk and pure cocoa powder instead.

foods.name: ginger beer/ginger ale
foods.notes: Check for HFCS. Brands with real sugar are better. Keep portions moderate.

foods.name: cola/soft drinks
foods.notes: European formulas use sugar (OK in small amounts). US imports with HFCS are worse. Check label.

foods.name: fennel tea
foods.notes: Moderate in fructans when brewed strong. Keep it weak.

foods.name: ginger tea
foods.notes: Low FODMAP. May help soothe digestive discomfort.

foods.name: protein powder (whey isolate)
foods.notes: Whey protein ISOLATE is low FODMAP (most lactose removed). Whey CONCENTRATE is higher in lactose. Check for inulin.

foods.name: protein powder (whey concentrate)
foods.notes: Contains significant lactose. Switch to whey isolate or plant-based protein.

foods.name: rice flour
foods.notes: Low FODMAP. Good wheat flour substitute for baking.

foods.name: potato starch
foods.notes: Low FODMAP. Good thickener.

foods.name: cornstarch
foods.notes: Low FODMAP. Common thickener.

foods.name: spring roll wrappers (rice paper)
foods.notes: Low FODMAP. Made from rice.

foods.name: soba noodles (100% buckwheat)
foods.notes: Low FODMAP if made from 100% buckwheat. Many contain wheat — check label.

foods.name: dried herbs mix (Provençal/Italian)
foods.notes: Plain dried herb mixes are low FODMAP. Check for onion/garlic powder in ingredients.

foods.name: oregano
foods.notes: Low FODMAP.

foods.name: dill
foods.notes: Low FODMAP.

foods.name: bay leaf
foods.notes: Low FODMAP. Essential in Belgian stews.

foods.name: nutmeg
foods.notes: Low FODMAP.

foods.name: vanilla extract
foods.notes: Low FODMAP.

foods.name: lemongrass
foods.notes: Low FODMAP. Great in Thai-style dishes.

foods.name: five-spice powder
foods.notes: Low FODMAP in normal seasoning amounts.

fructans.label: Fructans (Oligosaccharides)
fructans.description: Found in wheat, onion, garlic. Fermented by gut bacteria causing gas and bloating.

GOS.label: GOS (Galacto-oligosaccharides)
GOS.description: Found in legumes and beans. Can cause bloating and gas.

lactose.label: Lactose (Disaccharide)
lactose.description: Found in dairy. Requires lactase enzyme to digest.

excess fructose.label: Excess Fructose (Monosaccharide)
excess fructose.description: Found in honey, apples, high-fructose corn syrup. Issue is fructose exceeding glucose.

sorbitol.label: Sorbitol (Polyol)
sorbitol.description: Found in stone fruits and sugar-free products.

mannitol.label: Mannitol (Polyol)
mannitol.description: Found in mushrooms, cauliflower, and sugar-free products.
